findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on all resources ("Resource": "*"), violating least privilege. Compromise of this user's credentials would allow full control of compute, storage and serverless resources in the account, including data exfiltration from any S3 bucket and privilege escalation via EC2/Lambda role passing.

A permanent IAM access key is created for a user with broad permissions and no rotation mechanism. Long-lived static credentials are a common source of credential leakage; IAM roles or temporary credentials should be used instead. The secret is also stored in Terraform state in an accessible form.
No pgp_key is supplied, so the access key secret is stored unencrypted in the Terraform state file (and is retrievable via the secret attribute), exposing the credential to anyone with state access.
The access key secret attribute is exposed as a Terraform output without marking it sensitive, so it can appear in CLI output, CI/CD logs and downstream module consumers.
